Home / PBM devices

Formats, products and research use

PBM devices come in many forms.

Photobiomodulation is delivered with different light sources and applicators, from a small probe to a full-body bed. The device’s shape or advertised wattage alone does not show what dose reaches the target tissue or what evidence supports a particular use.

Browse device formatsDevices in the databaseOther light sourcesRegulatory authorizations

Device formats

From small applicators to full-body systems.

Product examples show the range of designs. They are not endorsements or a complete market catalogue.

Photobiomodulation device designs and example products
FormatWhat it looks likeExamples
Handheld probes and applicators
A small treatment head used near a specific area. Professional systems may use a laser probe or an LED cluster.
  • THOR LED and laser clusters
  • Laserpulse (Ibramed)
  • BTL-6000 and Mustang 2000 systems
Panels and lamps
Flat LED arrays, from small tabletop panels to larger panels for broader areas. Some have stands or wall mounts.
  • Hooga HG200 panel
  • MitoPRO X panels
  • Celluma PRO flexible panel
Flexible pads and wraps
Flexible LED surfaces, straps or modules positioned around a body area; some conform closely to the body.
  • Revival Wrap
  • Kineon MOVE+, a wearable LED-and-laser system
  • Pads, wraps, mats and pillows
Face masks
A close-fitting wearable light array shaped for the face. Wavelengths, fit and coverage differ by model.
  • Omnilux Contour Face
  • CurrentBody LED Face Mask, Series 2
Caps, helmets and headsets
Wearable devices shaped for the scalp or head. Some are hair caps; some pair head-mounted light modules with a nasal applicator.
  • HigherDOSE Red Light Hat
  • Vielight Neuro Gamma 4
Intranasal devices
A slim light emitter sits just inside one or both nostrils. Some devices are standalone; others pair a nasal module with a cranial headset.
  • Vielight Neuro Gamma 4 nasal module
  • Standalone intranasal LED applicators
Oral and dental devices
Toothbrush-shaped devices and mouthpieces deliver light close to oral tissues. These are specialized designs.
  • Oralucent Pro Edition, a sonic toothbrush
  • OrthoPulse, an intraoral near-infrared device
Full-body beds and pods
Large systems designed to expose much of the body at once, generally in a commercial or clinical setting.
  • NovoTHOR full-body bed
Wands and other shapes
Handheld wands, bulbs, bracelets and other less common shapes. Size, output and intended use vary.
  • LED or laser wands
  • Light bulbs and wearable accessories
  • Other forms listed in device catalogues and comparison sheets
Transcutaneous vascular PBM
Light is applied through the skin over a superficial vessel, often the radial artery, using a handheld probe or wrist-mounted holder. It is not delivered into the vessel.
  • DMC Therapy EC / Laser Therapy EC
  • Laser Duo (MMOptics)
  • Wrist-mounted radial-artery applicators
Intravascular PBM (ILIB)
A laser is coupled to a sterile optical fibre or catheter inserted into a vein, delivering light from within the vessel.
  • TAIEX YJ-ILIB-5 He–Ne laser system
  • Classcon helium–neon laser system
  • Laser source with a sterile fibre-optic catheter

The formats can overlap. In the literature, VPBM and ILIB labels are not always used consistently; these rows distinguish external light applied over a vessel from intravascular fibre-optic delivery by the physical route. A product name or design does not by itself show its output, intended use or supporting evidence. Current availability and specifications should be checked with the manufacturer.

Beyond PBM devices

Other light sources.

Red and near-infrared (NIR) light also occur in everyday sources.

Everyday light sources
Light sourceIn brief
Incandescent, halogen & heat lamps
Filament lamps emit a broad spectrum rich in red and NIR light, alongside heat.
Sunlight
A natural source of red and NIR light, together with other visible wavelengths and UV.
White LED & CFL bulbs
Mainly visible light; generally much less NIR than filament lamps. Different from dedicated PBM LEDs.

The spectrum alone does not establish a treatment dose or clinical benefit.

Common mix-ups

Not red-light therapy.

Heating, light filtering and evening lighting are different from PBM.

Products and settings sometimes confused with red-light therapy
Light sourceIn brief
Ceramic heaters & far-infrared saunas
Mainly longer-wave infrared heat, not red/NIR PBM. A separate PBM panel or NIR filament lamp is a different light source.
Blue-blocking glasses
Filter incoming light; they do not emit treatment light. Amber or red-tinted lenses are not red-light therapy.
Night Shift & similar screen settings
Shift a screen’s colours toward warmer tones, reducing the blue component of its light. This changes the display spectrum; it is not a PBM treatment.
Dim red evening lighting
Provides low-level room lighting in the evening, with less short-wavelength light. Its purpose is dim illumination, not a therapeutic PBM dose; a red colour alone does not make it red-light therapy.
